summary: CrisisConnect – AI Emergency Response & Resource Mapper web app. Detects user location, shows nearest hospitals, available blood donors, sends emergency alerts to nearby volunteers, and includes an AI chatbot for first-aid guidance. Features an SOS button (accessible before and after login) with extraordinary/advanced features. Tech stack: React/Tailwind frontend, Node.js/Firebase backend, Google Maps API, OpenAI API.
architectural_notes: Maps: Google Maps API for location and resource mapping
AI: OpenAI API for first-aid chatbot
SOS button must be accessible on all pages regardless of auth state
SOS pre-login: triggers emergency call/dial to emergency services; SOS post-login: notifies user-defined emergency contacts + emergency services
Blood type detection from proof documents must use precise regex/pattern matching to avoid false positives (e.g., matching 'A+' before 'B+')
Hospital data source: Overpass API (OpenStreetMap) used for real-time nearby hospital lookup by GPS coordinates, replacing static backend hospital records on map pages
leaflet-routing-machine integrated for in-map route rendering between user location and selected hospital using OSRM service
known_issues: Map page does not correctly show nearby hospitals with user location tracking and distance calculation
Map does not filter hospitals to within 5 km radius; no directions feature on hospital marker click
Volunteer registration form does not successfully add/save volunteer records
Volunteers are not displayed as markers on the ResourceMapPage map
Blood type detection from uploaded proof documents is incorrect — A+ is being misread as B+
Clicking a nearby hospital on the map does not show directions from the user's current location
Blood donor proof upload does not correctly analyze uploaded documents — returns random/incorrect blood type instead of parsing the actual value from the document

existing_features.title: Design and apply a bold emergency-response visual theme: deep charcoal dark background, vibrant red and amber accent colors, clean sans-serif typography, card-based layout with glowing alert indicators, and a persistent top navigation bar showing the app logo and a prominent SOS button.

Implement a persistent, highly visible SOS Emergency Button accessible on every page both before and after login. When triggered, it captures the user's current geolocation (browser Geolocation API) and records an SOS event in the backend with timestamp, coordinates, and optional user identity. Display a confirmation modal with countdown and cancel option.

Implement user authentication (register and login) using Internet Identity. Show a login/signup page with a clear call-to-action. After authentication, display the user's principal ID and a logout option in the navigation bar.

Build a real-time Emergency Resource Dashboard as the main page after login. Display summary cards for: total registered hospitals, available hospital beds count, registered blood donors by blood type, and active volunteer count. Cards should update when backend data changes.

Implement a Hospital Finder feature: display a list of registered hospitals with name, address, distance from user's location, available bed count, and emergency contact number. Allow filtering by distance and availability. Hospitals are stored and retrieved from the backend.

Implement a Blood Donor Registry: allow users to register as blood donors with fields: name, blood type (A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-), city, and contact number. Display a searchable list of donors filterable by blood type and city. Store all donor records in the backend.

Implement a Volunteer Management system: allow users to register as emergency volunteers with name, skills (first-aid, driving, medical, etc.), location (city), and availability status (active/inactive). Display a volunteer directory with filtering by skill and status. Store all volunteer records in the backend.

Implement an Emergency Alert Broadcasting feature: authenticated users can post an emergency alert with a type (flood, accident, medical, fire, other), description, and location. Alerts are stored in the backend with timestamp and user info. Display a live alert feed on the dashboard sorted by most recent, with color-coded severity badges.

Build an AI-powered First Aid Chatbot panel as a floating chat widget accessible from every page. The chatbot uses a rule-based / decision-tree approach (no external AI API) to guide users through first-aid steps for common emergencies: CPR, choking, bleeding, burns, fractures, and seizures. The widget opens as a slide-over panel with a chat interface.

Implement an interactive Nearest Resources Map page using Leaflet.js (open-source, no API key required) that plots hospitals and blood donor locations as map markers. User's geolocation is shown as a distinct marker. Clicking a marker shows a popup with the resource details.

Fix the ResourceMapPage to correctly request and track the user's geolocation using the browser Geolocation API (via the existing useGeolocation hook). On page load, automatically trigger location detection and display a loading state while acquiring coordinates. If geolocation is denied or unavailable, show a clear error message prompting the user to enable location access.

On the ResourceMapPage, after obtaining the user's geolocation, calculate the distance from the user's coordinates to each hospital using the existing haversine utility (frontend/src/utils/haversine.ts). Sort hospital markers by distance (nearest first). Display each hospital as a map marker with a popup showing: hospital name, address, available beds, contact number, and the calculated distance (formatted via the existing formatDistance helper).

Add a sidebar or overlay panel on the ResourceMapPage that lists nearby hospitals sorted by distance from the user's location. Each list item should show the hospital name, available beds (color-coded by availability), and the distance. Clicking a list item should pan/zoom the map to that hospital's marker and open its popup. This panel should be scrollable and styled consistently with the existing emergency dark theme.

Ensure the Leaflet map on ResourceMapPage initializes correctly with a valid center coordinate. When the user's geolocation is available, re-center the map to the user's coordinates. If geolocation is not yet available, initialize the map with a sensible default center (e.g., 0,0 or a known fallback) and re-center once location is acquired. Fix any issues with the map not rendering tiles or markers due to improper initialization or container sizing.

When the SOS button is triggered by an unauthenticated (pre-login) user, immediately prompt the browser to initiate a phone call to the universal emergency number (e.g., tel:112 or tel:911). Display a modal with a visible 'Call Emergency Services' button (rendered as an <a href='tel:112'> link) so the user can connect directly to emergency services without needing an account. The existing countdown/cancel flow should still capture geolocation and record the SOS event in the backend (anonymously), but the primary CTA must be the emergency call link.

Add an Emergency Contacts management feature for authenticated users. Provide a dedicated page or settings section (accessible from the navigation bar or user profile area) where a logged-in user can add, view, and remove emergency contacts. Each contact record must include: full name, phone number, and relationship (e.g., family, friend, colleague). Store emergency contacts in the backend associated with the authenticated user's principal ID.

When an authenticated user triggers the SOS button, after the countdown completes: (1) retrieve the user's stored emergency contacts from the backend and display them in the SOS confirmation modal as a list of 'Notify' entries showing each contact's name and phone number as a tel: call link; (2) also display a prominent 'Call Emergency Services (112)' tel: link button alongside the contacts. The SOS event must still be recorded in the backend with timestamp, geolocation coordinates, and the authenticated user's identity. Make it clear in the UI which contacts will be notified (via manual call links, since automated SMS/push is not supported) and provide a direct dial button for each.

On the ResourceMapPage, after obtaining the user's geolocation, filter the hospital list and map markers to show only hospitals whose haversine distance from the user's coordinates is ≤ 5 km. Hospitals beyond 5 km must not appear as markers on the map or in the sidebar list. Display a clear message (e.g., 'No hospitals found within 5 km') if no hospitals fall within the radius.

Fix the Leaflet map on ResourceMapPage so it renders tiles and markers correctly on first load. The map must initialize with a valid center coordinate (use a sensible fallback such as [20, 0] if geolocation is not yet available), re-center to the user's coordinates once geolocation is acquired, and properly size its container so tiles are not blank or misaligned.

When a user clicks on a hospital marker on the ResourceMapPage map (or on a hospital entry in the sidebar list), open the marker popup AND display a 'Get Directions' link that opens Google Maps directions from the user's current coordinates to the hospital's coordinates in a new browser tab, using the URL format: https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&origin={userLat},{userLng}&destination={hospitalLat},{hospitalLng}

Rewrite the ResourceMapPage Leaflet map initialization to guarantee correct rendering on first load: (1) initialize the map with a hardcoded fallback center of [20, 0] and zoom level 2 when geolocation is not yet available; (2) once geolocation is acquired, call map.setView() to re-center to the user's coordinates at zoom 13; (3) ensure the map container has an explicit CSS height (e.g., 100% filling its parent, which must itself have a fixed height) so Leaflet never renders blank or misaligned tiles; (4) call map.invalidateSize() after the container becomes visible or after any layout change.

Fix the useGeolocation hook integration in ResourceMapPage so that location detection is triggered automatically on page mount (call requestLocation() inside a useEffect with an empty dependency array). Display a loading spinner or status message ('Detecting your location…') while geolocation is in progress. If geolocation is denied or fails, show a clearly visible error banner ('Unable to detect location. Please enable location access in your browser settings.') instead of a blank or broken map.

Fix the 5 km hospital filtering logic on ResourceMapPage: after geolocation is acquired, use the haversine utility (frontend/src/utils/haversine.ts) to compute the distance from the user's coordinates to each hospital's lat/lng. Retain only hospitals where distance ≤ 5 km. Apply this filtered list to both the map markers and the sidebar panel. If the filtered list is empty, display the message 'No hospitals found within 5 km' in the sidebar and no hospital markers on the map. Ensure the filter re-runs whenever geolocation coordinates update.

Fix hospital marker rendering on the Leaflet map in ResourceMapPage: for each hospital within 5 km, create a Leaflet marker at the hospital's [lat, lng] coordinates. Each marker's popup must display the hospital name, address, available beds (color-coded: green ≥ 10, amber 1–9, red 0), contact number, and the calculated distance formatted via the formatDistance helper. Ensure all markers are added to the map after the map instance is fully initialized and the tile layer is loaded; remove and re-add markers when the filtered hospital list changes to avoid stale markers.

Fix the 'Get Directions' feature on ResourceMapPage: each hospital marker popup and each sidebar list item must include a 'Get Directions' link. The link must open in a new browser tab using the Google Maps directions URL format: https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&origin={userLat},{userLng}&destination={hospitalLat},{hospitalLng}. The user's current geolocation coordinates must be used as the origin; if geolocation is not yet available, the link should be disabled or hidden with a tooltip 'Enable location to get directions'.

Fix the sidebar panel on ResourceMapPage: ensure it lists all hospitals within 5 km sorted by distance (nearest first). Each list item must show the hospital name, available beds (color-coded), and formatted distance. Clicking a list item must call map.flyTo() (or map.setView()) to pan/zoom the map to that hospital's coordinates and programmatically open its popup. The sidebar must be scrollable when the list overflows its container and styled consistently with the existing emergency dark theme (charcoal background, red/amber accents).

Fix the volunteer registration form on VolunteerPage so that submitting a new volunteer record (name, skills, city, availability status) correctly calls the backend mutation and persists the data. After a successful submission, the volunteer must appear in the volunteer directory list without requiring a page reload. Display a success message on successful registration and a clear error message if the submission fails.

Add volunteer markers to the ResourceMapPage Leaflet map. For each registered volunteer who has a city that can be geocoded or who has lat/lng coordinates stored in the backend, display a distinct marker (visually different from hospital markers) on the map. Each volunteer marker popup must show the volunteer's name, city, skills (as badges), and availability status. Volunteers should be fetched from the backend using the existing useGetVolunteers query hook. If volunteer records do not contain lat/lng coordinates, derive approximate positions from their city field using a best-effort approach or display them in a dedicated sidebar section listing volunteers near the user.

Remove the 'Built with using caffeine.ai' footer text from all pages. Search all frontend layout and page components (including AppLayout.tsx, LoginPage.tsx, and any other page-level files) for any element rendering this text and delete it entirely. No footer attribution should appear anywhere in the application.

Update the Blood Donor registration form on BloodDonorPage.tsx to replace the manual blood type dropdown with a proof document upload step. Display accepted proof types to the user (e.g., 'Blood Test Report', 'Donor Card', 'Medical Certificate showing blood group'). Allow the user to upload one document (image: JPG/PNG, or PDF rendered as text). After the user selects a file, read its content client-side (use FileReader to extract text from text-based files, or display file name for images) and send the content to the backend. Show a 'Detected Blood Type: [X]' confirmation label after successful parsing. If the blood type cannot be auto-detected, show an inline error 'Could not detect blood type from the uploaded proof. Please upload a document clearly showing your blood group.' and do not allow form submission until a valid proof with detectable blood type is provided. Remove the manual blood type input field entirely from the registration form.

Update the Volunteer registration form on VolunteerPage.tsx to include a proof document upload step. Display accepted proof types to the user (e.g., 'Government ID', 'First Aid Certification', 'Medical License', 'Driving License', 'Any official credential'). Allow the user to upload one document (image or text file). Read the file client-side and send its content to the backend as `proofText`. The proof upload must be required — do not allow form submission without a file uploaded. Show the uploaded file name as confirmation once selected.

Add a volunteer detail view on VolunteerPage.tsx. When a user clicks on a volunteer card in the volunteer directory list, open a modal or expanded panel showing the volunteer's full details: name, city, skills (as badges), availability status, and proof document reference (display the file name or a 'Proof Submitted' indicator — do not render raw binary content). Style the detail view consistently with the existing emergency dark theme.

On the ResourceMapPage sidebar panel and hospital map marker popups, ensure each hospital entry prominently displays its full address. The address field must be clearly labeled (e.g., 'Address:') and displayed as a distinct line in both the sidebar list item and the Leaflet marker popup. On HospitalFinderPage.tsx, similarly ensure the full address is displayed prominently on each HospitalCard — verify the `address` field from the backend is rendered and not truncated.

Fix the blood type detection logic in BloodDonorPage.tsx: rewrite the client-side parser that extracts blood type from the uploaded proof document text. The regex/pattern matching must correctly identify all valid blood types (A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-) by searching for explicit patterns such as 'A+', 'Blood Group: A+', 'Blood Type A Positive', etc. The current bug misreads 'A+' as 'B+' — ensure the matching logic prioritizes the most specific and unambiguous match, tests patterns in the correct order (e.g., AB before A or B, and O before other types), and does not produce false positives. For image files (JPG/PNG) where text extraction is not possible, clearly prompt the user that the file name or a manually entered blood type confirmation is required. The 'Detected Blood Type' label must reflect the correctly parsed value before allowing form submission.

Completely rewrite the ResourceMapPage.tsx to implement a fully functional Leaflet.js + OpenStreetMap interactive map for nearby hospitals. The map must: (1) initialize with a hardcoded fallback center of [20, 0] at zoom level 2; (2) automatically request the user's geolocation on page mount via the existing useGeolocation hook; (3) once geolocation is acquired, call map.setView() to re-center at the user's coordinates at zoom 13 and call map.invalidateSize() to fix tile rendering; (4) use OpenStreetMap tile layer (https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png) — no API key required; (5) display a distinct user-location marker at the user's coordinates; (6) fetch all hospitals from the backend using the existing query hook; (7) use the haversine utility (frontend/src/utils/haversine.ts) to compute distance from user coordinates to each hospital's lat/lng; (8) show only hospitals within 5 km as map markers; (9) each hospital marker popup must display: hospital name, address (labeled 'Address:'), available beds (color-coded: green ≥10, amber 1–9, red 0), contact number, calculated distance (formatted via formatDistance), and a 'Get Directions' link opening Google Maps directions in a new tab using https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&origin={userLat},{userLng}&destination={hospitalLat},{hospitalLng}; (10) the map container must have an explicit CSS height so tiles never render blank or misaligned.

On the ResourceMapPage, implement a scrollable sidebar panel listing all hospitals within 5 km sorted by distance (nearest first). Each sidebar list item must show: hospital name, full address (labeled 'Address:'), available beds (color-coded: green ≥10, amber 1–9, red 0), formatted distance, and a 'Get Directions' link. Clicking a list item must call map.flyTo() to pan/zoom the map to that hospital's coordinates and programmatically open its marker popup. When geolocation is not yet available, disable 'Get Directions' links with a tooltip 'Enable location to get directions'. The sidebar must be scrollable when the list overflows and styled consistently with the existing emergency dark theme (charcoal background, red/amber accents).

On the ResourceMapPage, when a user clicks any nearby hospital marker on the Leaflet map OR any hospital entry in the sidebar list, immediately open the marker popup AND display a clearly visible 'Get Directions' button/link. This link must open Google Maps directions in a new browser tab using the URL format: https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&origin={userLat},{userLng}&destination={hospitalLat},{hospitalLng} — using the user's live geolocation coordinates as the origin and the hospital's stored lat/lng as the destination. If geolocation is not yet available, the 'Get Directions' link must be visually disabled (grayed out) with a tooltip reading 'Enable location to get directions'. Ensure the directions link is rendered as a proper anchor tag with target='_blank' and rel='noopener noreferrer'.

Completely rewrite the blood type detection logic in BloodDonorPage.tsx so that it reliably and correctly extracts the blood type from the uploaded proof document. The new parser must: (1) For text-based files (TXT, PDF rendered as text): apply a strict, ordered regex that tests for AB+, AB-, A+, A-, B+, B-, O+, O- in that exact priority order (most specific first) to avoid false positives — e.g., match 'AB' before 'A' or 'B', and 'O' only as a whole word/token. Search for patterns including bare symbols ('AB+', 'O-'), labeled formats ('Blood Group: A+', 'Blood Type: B-', 'Group: O+'), and spelled-out positivity/negativity ('A Positive', 'B Negative', 'O Positive'). (2) For image files (JPG/PNG) where text extraction is impossible: do NOT attempt regex on binary/base64 data — instead display a clear inline message: 'Image files cannot be analyzed automatically. Please type your blood type below.' and show a small manual blood type selector (A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-) that the user must confirm before the form can be submitted. (3) Display 'Detected Blood Type: [X]' confirmation label only when a blood type is positively identified. (4) If detection fails on a text file, show the error: 'Could not detect blood type from the uploaded proof. Please upload a document clearly showing your blood group.' and block form submission. (5) The detected or manually confirmed blood type must be sent to the backend correctly on form submission.

Rewrite ResourceMapPage.tsx to use the Overpass API (https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter) to fetch real nearby hospitals based on the user's live GPS coordinates instead of only querying the backend. On page mount, request the user's geolocation via the existing useGeolocation hook. Once coordinates are acquired, query Overpass for nodes with amenity=hospital or healthcare=hospital within a 10 km radius. Compute haversine distances from user to each result, sort by distance nearest-first, and display only hospitals within 5 km as map markers and in the sidebar list. Fall back gracefully (show 'No hospitals found within 5 km') if the Overpass query returns no results. The existing backend hospital data (via useGetHospitals) should still be merged/shown alongside Overpass results so registered hospitals are not lost.

On ResourceMapPage.tsx, integrate leaflet-routing-machine for in-map turn-by-turn directions. When the user clicks 'Get Directions' on a hospital marker popup or sidebar list item, render a Routing control using L.Routing.control with the OSRM service URL https://router.project-osrm.org/route/v1, plotting waypoints from the user's current coordinates to the selected hospital's lat/lng. The route line must be styled with the app's accent color (red/amber, e.g. #ef4444). Provide a 'Close Directions' button that removes the routing control from the map. Do not create duplicate routing controls — remove any existing control before adding a new one.

Update HospitalFinderPage.tsx to also fetch nearby hospitals from the Overpass API using the user's GPS coordinates (same query as ResourceMapPage: amenity=hospital or healthcare=hospital within 10 km radius), in addition to the backend-registered hospitals. Merge the two data sources (Overpass real-world + backend registered). Display distance, address extracted from Overpass tags (addr:street, addr:city, etc.), and phone number from Overpass tags (phone, contact:phone). Apply the existing emergency dark theme styling consistently (charcoal background, red/amber accents, glowing cards). Preserve all existing filtering (by distance, by availability) and the HospitalCard component structure.

On ResourceMapPage.tsx, each hospital marker popup and sidebar list item must display the address extracted from Overpass API tags (addr:housenumber + addr:street + addr:city + addr:postcode), phone number (from phone, contact:phone, or emergency:phone tags), opening hours (opening_hours tag), and a 24/7 Emergency badge if the emergency=yes or healthcare:emergency=yes tag is present. For hospitals sourced from the backend (not Overpass), continue showing the stored address and contact fields. All popup and sidebar content must be styled with the emergency dark theme (dark backgrounds, red/amber text accents, consistent typography).

Completely rewrite the blood type detection logic in BloodDonorPage.tsx. For text-based uploaded files (TXT or PDF read as text via FileReader): apply a strict priority-ordered regex testing AB+, AB-, A+, A-, B+, B-, O+, O- in that exact order (most specific first). Patterns must cover bare symbols (e.g. 'AB+'), labeled formats ('Blood Group: A+', 'Blood Type: B-', 'Group: O+'), and spelled-out forms ('A Positive', 'B Negative', 'O Positive'). For image files (JPG/PNG) where binary data cannot be parsed: do NOT run regex on raw binary/base64 content; instead display the inline message 'Image files cannot be analyzed automatically. Please select your blood type below.' and render a manual blood type selector (A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-) that the user must confirm before submission is allowed. Show 'Detected Blood Type: [X]' only when a type is positively identified. If detection fails on a text file, show 'Could not detect blood type from the uploaded proof. Please upload a document clearly showing your blood group.' and block form submission. The confirmed or detected blood type must be sent to the backend on form submission.

new_feature_requests.summary: User location detection and nearest hospital finder
Available hospital beds and blood donor availability display
Emergency alert system to notify nearby volunteers
AI chatbot for real-time first-aid guidance (OpenAI API)
SOS button accessible both before and after login
Google Maps integration for live resource mapping
User authentication (login/signup) system
Blood donor registration and search functionality
Real-time dashboard for emergency resources and volunteer coordination

Implement the Motoko backend actor with stable storage for: hospitals (id, name, address, lat, lng, bedsAvailable, contact), blood donors (id, name, bloodType, city, contact, registeredAt), volunteers (id, name, skills, city, isActive), SOS events (id, userId, lat, lng, timestamp), and emergency alerts (id, authorId, alertType, description, location, timestamp). Expose CRUD query and update functions for each entity.
SOS button pre-login: trigger emergency call (e.g., dial emergency number or prompt call to emergency services)
SOS button post-login: allow users to add emergency contacts/members; on SOS trigger, notify those specific persons AND emergency dial numbers

Extend the backend Motoko actor to support emergency contacts storage. Add a stable data structure to store emergency contacts keyed by user principal, where each contact has: id (generated), ownerPrincipal, name (Text), phone (Text), relationship (Text), and createdAt (Int timestamp). Expose the following update/query functions: addEmergencyContact (authenticated, adds a contact for the caller's principal), removeEmergencyContact (authenticated, removes by contact id for the caller's principal), getMyEmergencyContacts (authenticated query, returns the caller's contacts), and getEmergencyContactsByPrincipal (admin/internal query, returns contacts for a given principal for use during SOS dispatch).
Map: filter and show only available hospitals within 5 km of user location; clicking a hospital marker shows directions to it
Fix volunteer registration: adding a volunteer does not work (data not saved/submitted correctly)
Show volunteers on the ResourceMapPage map as markers, similar to hospitals
Remove 'Built with using caffeine.ai' footer text from all pages
Blood donor registration: require proof document upload (e.g., blood test report, donor card); auto-detect/extract blood group from the uploaded proof so user does not need to enter it manually
Volunteer registration: require proof document upload during registration; after registering, clicking on a volunteer entry shows their full details
Nearby hospitals on the map/list must display their full address prominently

Extend the backend Motoko actor to support a proof document reference on blood donor records. Add a `proofText` field (Text) to the BloodDonor type to store the submitted proof content (e.g., extracted text or filename). Add a `detectedBloodType` field (Text) that stores the blood type parsed from the proof. Update the `addBloodDonor` function to accept `proofText` and derive/store the blood type from it rather than requiring the caller to supply it directly.

Extend the backend Motoko actor to support a proof reference on Volunteer records. Add a `proofText` field (Text) to the Volunteer type to store proof content submitted during registration. The `addVolunteer` function must accept this `proofText` parameter and persist it with the volunteer record.
Fix blood group detection from uploaded proof documents: correctly parse and extract blood type (e.g., A+, B-, O+) from uploaded files; currently misreads A+ as B+

Implement Leaflet.js + OpenStreetMap on the Nearby Hospitals page: show user location marker, fetch and display nearby hospitals as markers, calculate distances using lat/lng (Haversine), and list hospitals sorted by distance

Integrate working Overpass API-based hospital detection (real GPS location, nearby hospitals fetched from OpenStreetMap, distance calculated via Haversine) into both HospitalFinderPage and ResourceMapPage, styled with the CrisisConnect dark emergency theme; also includes leaflet-routing-machine for in-map turn-by-turn directions

Fix blood donor proof document analysis: uploaded proof documents must be properly parsed to extract the correct blood type (not random); image files should prompt manual selection; text files must use strict ordered regex (AB+/AB- before A/B, O as whole token)
